chapter: Casa, Zeb Lenard and Little Joe
title: Ernest Kelly, uniforms and diabetes
summary: Asked why Zeb and Ernest Kelly are linked, Vincent recalls Ernest Kelly's size, the uniform tailor's charge, his diabetes and death, and that he went to Mexico with them.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Ask him why he's got Zeb and Ernest Kelly together. Zeb was a fine fella. You see what?

He never disappointed me. He said, why come you got Zeb and Chris Kelly together? Ernest Kelly. Ernest Kelly. Well, that's not just coming to my mind, you know. Ernest Kelly. Did they work together? He told me about Ernest Kelly, didn't he? Did they ever work together? You know, that's what I told. When we were playing together, we had to get our uniform, you know. And so I asked, I asked the man, I asked the man, why did he charge me the same thing that charged Eddie? I went, Ernest. He said, well, I said, you can take Ernest's coat and make me a suit and two pounds extra pounds. And he said, well, I had to go through the same thing with a small man like we do with a big man. I had to pay, you know. Ernest had diabetes, because one day he goes, then he gets to cut the other one. And he died. He was big, too. He had a uncle named Jim Benavis. He was trying to go through the tooth. He went to Mexico with us. You can't get that the weekend, get it. Put it all in there every day. And it burn out, you know. It ain't stuck in the cotton good. That's right. I said, I'm gonna take all the cotton out and put it in so it didn't keep it. Yeah, good week.
